content.thinking:
I'm writing out the JSON spec with the decision order: reject, escalate, return, incomplete, then approve, with order_sop set to "2.1". For the unknowns case, I'm using the sentence from SOP 2.2 that a claim with an unknown required fact cannot be approved, and mapping it to "incomplete."

I'm now weighing whether to add a default approve rule, since no explicit SOP sentence says to approve when nothing else applies, though approve reads as the fallback under the most-severe-outcome ordering.

I'm weighing whether a default approve rule with an empty condition is justified, since the SOP only implies approve as the fallback through the most-severe-outcome ordering in 2.1. I'm considering citing section 1 for the point that every claim receives exactly one outcome, to support including that fallback.

I'm settling on the approve rule as the default: approve only if nothing above it applies, so I'll cite section 1 for the outcome wording. The 4.5 pre-approved airfare rule runs into the escalation in 4.4, and since approve sits last, that escalation wins and the 4.5 rule can't actually change the result.

I'm now checking the 3.1 rule: reject when days_to_submit is at least 61, which fits the 60-day limit. Next, 3.2 means a self-approved claim gets rejected. For 3.3, I'm mapping the 5000 USD threshold without a director signature to escalate, using director_signed being "no" as the condition.

I'm now writing the rules for line-level checks: a return rule for any line with an amount band of 75 or more and no itemised receipt, a return rule for any alcohol line, and escalation for gift lines where the recipient is an official. I'm also adding an escalation for airfare lines in business or first class, and I'm still deciding how to handle a claim with no lines at all.

I'm adding maps for the cabin wording, so "business-class" becomes business and "first-class" becomes first.

I'm checking the remaining checks against the SOP wording: the 60-day window, the receipt requirement and the pre-approval wording all line up with the facts I've already defined. Next I'm confirming the sections I still need to account for, including whether the default approve rule should cite section 1.

I'm checking the wording for the 3.3 and 4.3 rules, and I'm settling that the 4.4 airfare rule only looks at the cabin when the line is airfare. I'm also planning the default approve rule with an empty condition, which should be valid as an always-true fallback.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the claim cannot be approved.

lines.unknown_when_empty: what lines (receipts or expenses) the claim has
lines.text: A claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense.

rules.text: Claims must be submitted within 60 days of the earliest expense on them. Reject a claim submitted 61 days or more after its earliest expense.
A claim's approver must not be the employee who submitted it. Reject a self-approved claim.
A claim totalling $5,000 or more needs the Finance Director's sign-off. Without it, escalate.
Every line of $75 or more needs an itemised receipt. If a receipt is missing or has not been attached, return the claim.
Alcohol is not reimbursable. Return any claim with a line for alcohol.
A gift to a government official must be reviewed under the anti-bribery policy. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class and first-class airfare must be reviewed. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class airfare pre-approved in writing by the Finance Director may be approved.
Every claim receives exactly one outcome:

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes and that a claim is a list of lines. The lines collection comes from this section. No section states when to approve. default-approve makes Approve the outcome when no other rule applies, which 2.1's ordering implies. A person should confirm this reading.
Sets the order of outcomes, most severe first (order / order_sop).
Sets what happens when a required fact is unknown: the claim cannot be approved, which section 1 calls Incomplete (unknowns).

Translated as written. It conflicts with 4.4: any line it covers also triggers 4.4's escalate, which outranks approve under 2.1. So this rule can never decide a claim. A person should decide how 4.4 and 4.5 relate.

problems: The word map for cabin has "Business-class", which no case word can match; write it trimmed and in lower case.
The word map for category has "Alcohol", which no case word can match; write it trimmed and in lower case.
